obtained.how: the publisher's own free copy (Lakes Environmental Association website), 26-page PDF with a text layer

bibliography.note: cover: "Winter Monitoring Report, Lakes Environmental Association, 2026"; 31 trips to 16 lakes in the greater Bridgton area, January–March 2026

claims.claim: ice 31–50 cm at 16 lakes around Bridgton in 2026, with maxima of 35–75 cm in 2018–2025
claims.quote: Measured ice thickness ranged from 31 to 50 cm (12.2–19.7 in; Fig. 1)
claims.conditions: deep-site holes, visits from mid-January to early March 2026 (Fig. 1); past maxima "35–75 cm during 2018–2025"; ice mostly clear (black) in 2026, with less white ice or slush than previous years
claims.note: the 2026 visits span mid-January to early March, so the range is mid- to late-winter rather than strictly late-winter

claims.claim: light just under the ice was about 1–12 % of surface irradiance
claims.quote: levels just beneath the ice layer varied from about 1 to 12% of surface irradiance
claims.conditions: LI-COR LI-192 quantum sensor under ice, hole covered with screening; whole 2026 season

claims.claim: the under-ice light fell as snow deepened from none to about 20 cm
claims.source_value: Fig. 2: snow depths ran from 0 to about 28 cm; light fell from ~10–12 % with no snow to ~3 % by ~10–15 cm of snow and then levelled off, with scatter (two points near 9 % at ~21 and ~25 cm); the report says the relationship "was not as clear as in other years" because snow was present on almost every visit
claims.quote: This relationship was not as clear as in other years, probably because snow
claims.conditions: per-visit points with a smoothed fit (read on the page image)
claims.note: write "falling from ~10 % without snow to ~3 % under 10–28 cm of snow"

claims.claim: chlorophyll often peaked within a few meters of the ice
claims.quote: often showed a peak in fluorescence within a few meters of the ice-water
claims.conditions: sonde chlorophyll fluorescence profiles (a relative measure), sometimes peaking directly under the ice when snow cut the light; declined as winter progressed

claims.claim: winter chlorophyll in 16 lakes near Bridgton was 0.4–7.2 µg/L
claims.quote: Winter 2026 lake chlorophyll-a measurements ranged from 0.4 to 7.2 ppb
claims.conditions: extracted chlorophyll-a on core-tube samples integrating ice to 10 m (or to 1 m above bottom); Holt Pond top 0.5 m; mostly near or below each lake's summer average

claims.claim: under the ice the column is inversely stratified, temperature rising quickly through the first meter and then slowly toward 4 °C at the bottom
claims.quote: increased rapidly with depth within the first meter or so (a stratified layer)
claims.conditions: sonde profiles at deep sites; sometimes a mixed layer with little change with depth; the report notes water is densest at 4 °C so the warmest water is at the bottom

claims.claim: surface water under the ice was near saturation, but 5 of 16 lakes had bottom water at or below 2 mg/L on at least one visit
claims.quote: Five lakes had hypoxic (DO of 2 mg/L or less) deep waters
claims.conditions: "Surface (at the ice-water interface) DO concentrations were mostly near saturation"; deep-site profiles in lakes mostly deeper than Hot Brook (e.g. Bear Pond to ~20 m); the five were Bear, Highland, Holt, Keoka and Middle

notes: Everything checks but the snow range in §3.1.4 (the snow went to ~28 cm, and the light levelled off at ~3 % beyond ~10–15 cm). Context for the rewrite: these are deep-site measurements in mostly deeper, clear lakes (winter Secchi 3.0–9.3 m; TP 4.1–13.9 ppb), so they bound rather than represent Hot Brook. Most lakes iced in early December 2025 (some only in early January 2026) and were ice free by early April; ice grew 2.7–11.3 cm between visits.
